title: Union Health Ministry Showcases Flagship Health Programmes and Initiatives at 45th India International Trade Fair 2026
subtitle:
Dr. M. Srinivas, Member, NITI Aayog, Inaugurates Health Pavilion; Emphasises Preventive Healthcare and Healthy Lifestyle Choices to Address Rising Burden of Non-Communicable Diseases
Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava Attends Inauguration of Health Pavilion at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi
Health Pavilion Themed ‘युवा भारत, स्वस्थ भारत’ Highlights Preventive Healthcare, Healthy Lifestyles and Youth Participation in Building a Healthier Nation
39 Stalls Representing 24 National Health Programmes and Organisations Showcase Government's Healthcare Initiatives, Achievements and Services
Interactive Activities, Live CPR Demonstrations, Health Awareness Sessions and Dedicated Kids’ Zone to Engage Visitors and Promote Healthy Living
body_text: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) is showcasing its flagship health programmes, key achievements and public healthcare initiatives through a dedicated Health Pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 , being organised by the India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO) at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, from 14th to 27th November 2026. The Health Pavilion was inaugurated today by Dr. M. Srinivas, Member, NITI Aayog, in the presence of Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Union Health Secretary; Dr. Rajiv Bahl, Secretary, Department of Health Research (DHR) and Director General, Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), Shri Sunil Kumar Barnwal, Chief Executive Officer, National Health Authority (NHA), and other senior officials of the Ministry. The Ministry's participation in the prestigious annual event provides an important platform to connect directly with citizens, showcase the Government's wide-ranging healthcare initiatives and promote greater public awareness about preventive healthcare, early diagnosis and healthier lifestyles. ‘ युवा भारत , स्वस्थ भारत’ : Promoting a Culture of Preventive Healthcare This year's Health Pavilion, themed ‘युवा भारत, स्वस्थ भारत’, places special emphasis on preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyle practices and the active involvement of young people in building a healthier and more resilient India. The theme reflects the importance of encouraging healthy habits from an early age, strengthening health awareness and empowering citizens to make informed choices about their physical and mental well-being. Through informative exhibits, interactive demonstrations and public engagement activities, the Pavilion seeks to make healthcare information accessible, relatable and engaging, particularly for youth, children and families. Addressing the gathering, Dr. M. Srinivas highlighted the increasing burden of Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs) and lifestyle-related health conditions, underscoring the need for a stronger focus on preventive healthcare and the adoption of healthier lifestyle practices. He emphasised the importance of public awareness, early detection and timely medical intervention in preventing and managing NCDs, while encouraging citizens to take greater responsibility for their health through informed lifestyle choices. Dr. Srinivas observed that the Health Pavilion offers a valuable opportunity for citizens to learn about common health risks, understand preventive measures and familiarise themselves with various Government healthcare programmes and services. He encouraged visitors, particularly young people and families, to actively participate in the Pavilion's activities and use the opportunity to enhance their understanding of health and well-being. Union Health Ministry Brings 24 Health Programmes and Organisations Under One Roof The Health Pavilion brings together 24 National Health Programmes, Programme Divisions and participating organisations, represented through 39 stalls spread across 989 square metres on the Ground Floor of Hall No. 4 at Bharat Mandapam. The Pavilion offers visitors a comprehensive overview of India's public healthcare initiatives, covering primary healthcare, disease prevention and control, immunisation, maternal and child health, digital health services, mental healthcare, food safety, organ donation and other important areas of public health. Flagship initiatives and services being showcased include Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, Ayushman Bharat–Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana through the National Health Authority, eSanjeevani, the Universal Immunisation Programme, Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram, TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, Tele-MANAS and several national disease prevention and control programmes. The Pavilion also facilitates direct engagement between visitors and representatives of the Ministry's Programme Divisions and participating organisations, enabling citizens to learn about healthcare services, seek information and develop a better understanding of Government health initiatives. Interactive Activities to Make Health Awareness Engaging and Accessible A wide range of informative and participatory activities has been organised throughout the Pavilion to encourage public engagement and promote awareness about preventive healthcare. These include live Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) demonstrations, health awareness sessions, Nukkad Natak, health talk shows and interactive quiz programmes. The activities are designed to communicate important public health messages in simple and engaging ways, while enhancing awareness about disease prevention, early detection, emergency response and healthy lifestyle practices. Dedicated Kids’ Zone Encourages Screen-Free Learning and Healthy Recreation A special Kids’ Zone has also been established at the Health Pavilion, featuring traditional games and recreational activities for children. With an emphasis on largely screen-free engagement, the zone seeks to encourage physical activity, social interaction and learning through play. The initiative aims to familiarise children with the importance of healthy habits while providing an enjoyable and engaging environment for families visiting the Pavilion. Special Focus on TB Awareness, Screening and Community Participation A dedicated TB stall has been established to raise awareness about tuberculosis and inform visitors about prevention, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment and the range of services available under the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP). As part of the activities, TB screening is being conducted using AI-enabled handheld X-ray technology, while a Medical Officer is providing medical consultations and guidance to visitors. The stall is also facilitating the registration of Ni-kshay Mitras, encouraging individuals and organisations to support persons affected by TB, including through the provision of nutritional food baskets. Public awareness activities, including Nukkad Natak, magic shows and interactions with the TB mascot, are being organised to communicate key messages on early detection, timely treatment, nutritional support and community participation in the fight against tuberculosis. The initiative highlights the importance of collective action and citizen participation in advancing the goal of a TB-Mukt Bharat. Strengthening Public Awareness and Citizen Participation for a Healthier India The Health Pavilion at IITF 2026 reflects the Ministry's continued emphasis on bringing health information and public healthcare initiatives closer to citizens. By combining informative exhibits, practical demonstrations, interactive activities and direct public engagement, the Pavilion seeks to encourage greater awareness about preventive healthcare and empower individuals and families to make healthier lifestyle choices. The Ministry's participation also reinforces the importance of youth engagement, community participation and informed health choices in building a Swasth Bharat.
